title: The spread, revived
summary: Round 2's handover spread, which you approved, rebuilt on one dark surface. There's no side bar now. Six documents cross the Handover line in a single row, and directly under each one sits what it is, the problem from the letter it ends (struck out) and what replaces it. The section is about a quarter shorter than round 3.
story: This is the payoff. The six problems from the founder's letter are struck out, word for word and in the same order, once the six documents that end them have crossed onto your side, so the page closes on you owning the system and hands the method a clean 'now, where it starts'.
motion: Standalone (plays once, finished by about 5.1s): the heading rises as on every section. The panel fades in and the Handover line draws top to bottom. The six dashed drafts are laid onto a small stack at the panel's left end, 01 first and 06 on top. Meanwhile the six names, their tags and the six old problem lines fade in under six empty dotted places on your side; the new lines wait.

The spread, at about 2.1s (the move you approved in round 2): the stack fans out across the Handover line in one row. The top sheet leaves first and the rest follow a beat apart, all taking the same time, so the sheets only ever separate: none passes over another sheet or over a label. As each sheet crosses the line, its edge turns from dashed to solid and its rough draft page becomes the finished page, split exactly at the line. Rough notes become a message hierarchy, two plays become six, a raw list becomes a table, conditions gain actions, empty panels light up, and one quarter's pile spreads across four. A dotted outline is all that's left where the drafts stood.

The payoff, in reading order: once all six are across, the old lines are struck out left to right, 01 to 06, each by a drawn hairline, and each new line rises in beneath its struck one. Then the small title block lands at the bottom-right as the sign-off: 'Yours · 06 of 06'.

On the live page: the heading and the waiting stack arrive when the section scrolls in. The spread waits until the whole row of sheets is on screen, so nothing crosses out of sight, and then it plays once. Nothing loops. Hovering an asset lifts its sheet slightly and brightens its edge.

With reduced motion, on phones, or if the animation library fails to load, the finished state shows at once: all six handed over and every old line struck. Even with scripts off, the old lines still render struck.
addressed: "I don't like the way things are laid out in this one": I went back to the layout you approved in round 2, 'The handover, spread'. It's one full-width panel with six documents in a row, crossing a vertical Handover line, now with round 3's struck-out payoff built directly into it.

"Especially the black bar kind of thing": the dark side column is gone. The whole section is one surface, and Kelwin's side is just a small dotted outline and a short arrow at the panel's left end, with the key under it. That's enough to explain the dashed-to-solid change without taking a column of the page.

"It's making the main content take up too much vertical space": the section is 987px tall at desktop width, against 1,296px in round 3, about a quarter shorter. The six assets now run across the full width instead of being squeezed into nine columns. The heading is one statement tall because the opening paragraph and the handover test sit beside it, not under it.

Your standing note that artifacts must be clear at first glance, never an afterthought: each document is drawn as its own kind of page (a message hierarchy, a set of plays, a data table, if-then rules, a dashboard, a quarterly plan). Each one visibly turns from a rough draft into the finished page as it crosses the line, and the old problem it ends is struck out right underneath it.

Everything you approved is kept: 'When we leave, the system stays.', the 'Same team, same market' opening, the handover test, the three capability groups and the six tags. The six struck lines are the letter's margin lines, word for word, numbered 01 to 06 the same way, so the setup in the letter pays off here.
notes: V.html is generated: edit scratchpad/redesign/work/handover-V/gen.mjs and re-run it (node work/handover-V/gen.mjs) rather than editing V.html by hand. Geometry is shared between gen.mjs and V.css: Kelwin's zone KZ 146px (--kz), datum track DZ 36px (--dz, datum at its centre = 164px into the grid), sheet 96×136 (--sw/--sh, 1:1.41), plate padding 22px, so each asset column is 165px (16px in-pair gaps, 24px between capability pairs). The head's lede and note start one gutter before col 8 (x 819 on the 1440 stage), on the same vertical as sheet 04. Each sheet is drawn twice in its slot: a draft copy (dashed edge, rough page) and an owned copy (solid edge, finished page). During the spread V.js translates each sheet from the stack and clips the two copies at the datum every frame. At rest the draft copy is clipped away in CSS, so the default CSS is the final state. Positions use offsetLeft/offsetTop chains, which ignore transforms and the homepage zoom. Strikes are SVG lines measured in JS, one per rendered line. They are rebuilt on resize, on fonts loading and on a skin change (MutationObserver on html[data-skin]), because a skin change can re-break a line without resizing its box. A 1px line-through is the no-JS fallback only (.is-ink removes it). The datum and tick are lifted above the travelling sheets only while .is-deal is set. The ≤760px rules hide the datum and deck with visibility rather than display:none: the tall-element screenshot briefly trips the narrow media query, and display:none restarts their entrance animations, which blanked them in the capture. Surface: graphite with a --panel plate, the approved round-2 look. The paper principle above stays the single bright pause, and the handover and method share graphite because they are one movement (the exit, then the entry). Because graphite now meets graphite, method should carry .ac-sec--ruled at the cut; this slot draws no bottom rule of its own, to avoid a doubled hairline. The section's bottom padding is trimmed by 24px because the title block hangs below the plate; the plate still has about 150px of air beneath it. Deviations from STORY §3·07, all forced by the round-4 note or the motion: (1) the split-surface archetype is replaced by round 2's single plate (his note wins over STORY's archetype); (2) no caption band or segmented control, and the spread plays once; (3) the strikes play 01→06 once all six have landed, not per crossing. A no-pass spread from a left-hand stack must cross 06 first, so tying each strike to its crossing would read right to left. (4) The title block adds a 'Specimen' cell (illustrative drawings) and lands as a whole at the end rather than fading in one cell, which would leave an empty cell mid-sequence. ★ lines are kept verbatim; no copy changed and nothing is added beyond 'Specimen'. Lint: PASS with no warnings in both skins at 987px. The round-3 'Kelwin's side' label stays a plain caps caption (no red square), so the section keeps family punctuation only: two label squares and the rule, plus its one red, the datum tick.
